name: Fairino FR3 cell 0.4 nozzle
printer_notes: Fairino FR3 cell (docs/nonplanar/kinematics/fr3): a Fairino FR3 6-DOF arm carries an inline direct-drive extruder and hotend and prints onto a tilt-rotate positioner in front of it: A about machine X, +-135 deg at 120 deg/s, C continuous at 360 deg/s on the trunnion, heated D80 build puck on a D30 spindle 142 mm long, the puck surface on the A axis (the part may overhang the puck; part envelope D160 x 100 mm). Layout table_ac: the tool stays vertical in the machine frame and the positioner turns the part so each chunk's build direction points up (gravity-aligned, up to 135 deg from the plate normal). G-code: XYZ is the TCP in the positioner's fixed frame, origin where the A and C axes meet (the puck centre), mm; A and C are the positioner angles in degrees (work frame -> machine: Rx(A) Rz(C)); E relative; rotary_tool_length 142.34 is the tip-to-flange length and rotary_tool_mount puts the flange 142.34 above the TCP at home, so XYZ reads the TCP; G93 inverse-time F on moves that turn A or C, G94 mm/min otherwise. The FR3 converter maps it to joint trajectories. Arm limits 300 mm/s, 3000 mm/s^2 and 8 mm/s jerk (fitted so the slicer's estimate matches the FR3 converter's joint-limited corners within 5 % on five parts); calibrated=false.
